adsbProxy.label: Daten-Proxy
adsbProxy.tipBuiltIn: Cloudflare-Worker für Flugdaten & OpenStreetMap. Leer lassen = eingebauter Proxy.

steps.2: Key unter „Developers“ nach dem Login kopieren

camdirToken.label: Kamera-Richtungen: Token
camdirToken.tip: Admin-Token, mit dem du Blickrichtungen von Kameras ändern darfst (nur du kennst ihn).

steps.1: Im Worker das Secret ADMIN_TOKEN setzen (lange Zufallszeichenfolge)
steps.2: Dieselbe Zeichenfolge hier einfügen – sie bleibt nur in diesem Browser

camdirWorker.label: Kamera-Richtungen (Worker)

steps.1: proxy/camdir-worker.js als Cloudflare-Worker deployen, KV-Namespace als CAMDIR binden (siehe README „Kamera-Richtungen“)

camdirWorker.tipBuiltIn: Eigener Cloudflare-Worker mit korrigierten Kamera-Blickrichtungen. Leer lassen = eingebauter Worker.

steps.2: Key per E-Mail erhalten und hier einfügen

googleRoutes.label: Google Routes
googleRoutes.tip: Routenplanung mit Google Routes (Live-Verkehr, beste Abdeckung). Ohne Key nutzt Orbis kostenlose OpenStreetMap-Dienste.

steps.1: In der Google Cloud Console ein Projekt mit Abrechnung anlegen (es gibt ein monatliches Gratis-Kontingent)
steps.3: Unter „Anmeldedaten“ einen API-Key erstellen und auf „HTTP-Referrer“ (diese Seite) sowie auf die Routes API beschränken
steps.4: Key hier einfügen – danach unter Route planen „Google Routes“ wählen

steps.2: Im Dashboard unter „API Keys“ einen Key erzeugen

steps.3: Hier einfügen – danach unter Grundkarte „Mapbox Satellit“ wählen
Hier einfügen – danach unter Grundkarte „MapTiler Satellit“ wählen

nps.label: US National Park Service
nps.tip: Webcams der US-Nationalparks (ohne Key: gemeinsamer Snapshot).

steps.1: Formular ausfüllen – Key kommt sofort nach dem Absenden per E-Mail

steps.2: Key nach der Registrierung im Account kopieren

ors.label: OpenRouteService
ors.tip: Routenplanung mit OpenRouteService (gute Rad- und Fußrouten, 2 000 Routen/Tag gratis).

steps.3: Hier einfügen – der Key kann bis zu 1 Std. inaktiv bleiben

pushWorker.label: Fahrplan-Worker (Verspätungen & Push)
pushWorker.tip: Eigener Cloudflare-Worker für den Fahrplan: Bahn-Verspätungen (DB-Daten) und Benachrichtigungen für Pendler-Verbindungen.

steps.1: proxy/fahrplan-push-worker.js als Cloudflare-Worker deployen, KV und Schlüssel einrichten (siehe README „Fahrplan: Bahn-Verspätungen & Benachrichtigungen“)

pushWorker.tipBuiltIn: Eigener Cloudflare-Worker für den Fahrplan: Bahn-Verspätungen (DB-Daten) und Benachrichtigungen für Pendler-Verbindungen. Leer lassen = eingebauter Worker.

steps.2: API-Key laut Spezifikation (PDF) bzw. Anforderung verwenden

radarHost.label: Radar-Server
radarHost.tip: Eigener RainViewer-kompatibler Server statt der begrenzten RainViewer-Quelle.

steps.1: LibreWXR selbst hosten (open source, RainViewer- Ersatz)
steps.2: Server-URL (https://…) hier eintragen – kein Schlüssel nötig

tomtom.label: TomTom Traffic
tomtom.tip: Live-Verkehrslage (Stau/Fluss) für die Verkehrssimulation. Ohne Key fahren die Fahrzeuge mit Normaltempo.

steps.1: Kostenloses Konto bei TomTom Developer anlegen
steps.2: Unter „Keys“ einen API-Key mit „Traffic API“ kopieren (Free: 2.500 Anfragen/Tag)

trafiklab.label: Trafiklab
trafiklab.tip: Busse & Bahnen in Schweden (GTFS Regional Realtime).

steps.2: Projekt anlegen → API „GTFS Regional Realtime“ hinzufügen → Key

trafikverket.label: Trafikverket
trafikverket.tip: Straßenkameras in Schweden (ohne Key: gemeinsamer Snapshot).

utah511.label: UDOT Traffic
utah511.tip: Verkehrskameras UDOT Traffic (ohne Key: gemeinsamer Snapshot).

steps.2: Im Profil API-Key (KeyId) erzeugen und hier einfügen

sun.desc: Our star – a yellow dwarf holding 99.86% of the mass of the solar system.

mercury.desc: The smallest and the planet closest to the Sun, without any notable atmosphere.

venus.desc: The hottest planet – a dense CO₂ atmosphere produces an extreme greenhouse effect.

earth.desc: Our home planet. Zooming in opens the weather map.

moon.desc: Because of its tidally locked rotation, the Earth's moon always shows us the same side.

mars.desc: The red planet with the highest volcano (Olympus Mons) and the largest canyon in the solar system.

jupiter.desc: The largest planet – a gas giant with the Great Red Spot, a storm raging for centuries.

saturn.desc: The ringed planet – its rings consist of chunks of ice and are only about 10 m to 1 km thick.

uranus.desc: An ice giant that practically orbits the Sun lying on its side.

neptune.desc: The outermost planet – with the fastest winds in the solar system.

pluto.desc: A dwarf planet in the Kuiper Belt, visited by New Horizons in 2015.

ceres.desc: The largest body in the asteroid belt and the only dwarf planet in the inner solar system – explored by the Dawn spacecraft in 2015.

vesta.desc: The second-largest body in the asteroid belt, with the giant Rheasilvia impact basin at its south pole – mapped by Dawn in 2011/12.

eris.desc: The most massive known dwarf planet beyond Neptune, discovered in 2005 – its discovery led to a new definition of "planet". No surface map available.

haumea.desc: A fast-rotating, egg-shaped dwarf planet in the Kuiper Belt, with a ring and two moons. No surface map available.

makemake.desc: A bright, reddish dwarf planet in the Kuiper Belt. No surface map available.

eros.desc: A near-Earth asteroid, discovered in 1898 and orbited by NEAR Shoemaker in 2000/01 – the first asteroid on which a spacecraft landed.

bennu.desc: A carbon-rich, near-Earth asteroid – OSIRIS-REx took a sample here in 2020 and brought it back to Earth in 2023.

itokawa.desc: A near-Earth, peanut-shaped asteroid – visited by Hayabusa in 2005; in 2010 asteroid samples returned to Earth for the first time.

kleopatra.desc: A bone-shaped metallic asteroid in the main belt with two small moons.

geographos.desc: An extremely elongated near-Earth asteroid – one of the most stretched bodies in the solar system.

toutatis.desc: A near-Earth asteroid with a chaotic tumbling motion; China's Chang'e 2 flew past it in 2012.

mithra.desc: A near-Earth Apollo-class asteroid, mapped by radar.

golevka.desc: A small near-Earth asteroid – the Yarkovsky effect (orbit change by heat radiation) was measured here for the first time.

hw1.desc: A double-asteroid-like "contact binary" made of two merged bodies, mapped by radar.

iss.desc: The International Space Station – position live from current orbital data (CelesTrak).

hubble.desc: The famous space telescope – position live from current orbital data (CelesTrak).

voyager1.desc: The farthest human-made object. Visited Jupiter and Saturn.

voyager2.desc: The only probe to have visited all four gas giants (Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune).

newhorizons.desc: Explored Pluto and the Kuiper Belt object Arrokoth.

pioneer10.desc: The first probe to cross the asteroid belt and visit Jupiter.

jwst.fact.location: Lagrange point L2, 1.5 million km from Earth
jwst.desc: The largest space telescope, observing in infrared.

soho.fact.location: Lagrange point L1 between Earth and Sun
soho.desc: A solar observatory of ESA and NASA.

parker.fact.sunProximity: 6.2 million km – closer than anything ever before
parker.desc: It flies through the corona of the Sun.

juno.desc: Orbits Jupiter on a polar trajectory.

perseverance.text: Collects rock samples for a later return to Earth. Its onboard helicopter Ingenuity completed 72 flights (2021–2024).

ingenuity.fact.firstFlight: 19 April 2021 – first powered flight on another planet
ingenuity.desc: The Mars helicopter – the map shows all flight paths; the dot marks its last landing spot.

lro.desc: Maps the Moon at the highest resolution.

europaclipper.desc: To study the Jupiter moon Europa for habitability.

juice.desc: ESA mission to the icy moons Ganymede, Callisto and Europa.

apollo11.crew: Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin (in orbit: Michael Collins)
apollo11.text: The first crewed Moon landing. "That's one small step for a man, one giant leap for mankind." The laser reflector is still used for distance measurement.

apollo12.text: Bull's-eye landing just 180 m from the Surveyor 3 probe – parts of it were brought back to Earth.

apollo14.text: Alan Shepard hit two golf balls here with an improvised club.

apollo15.region: Hadley Rille at the foot of the lunar Apennines
apollo15.text: First landing with a rover. David Scott dropped a hammer and a feather at the same time – without air, both hit the ground at the same time.

apollo16.text: The only landing in the central highlands. Charles Duke left a photo of his family on the Moon.

apollo17.text: The most recent humans on the Moon to date. Harrison Schmitt, a geologist, was the first scientist there.

luna9.text: First soft landing on another celestial body and first photos of the lunar surface.

surveyor1.text: First soft Moon landing by the USA – a dress rehearsal for Apollo.

luna16.text: First robotic sample return: 101 g of lunar soil came back to Earth.

luna17.text: Carried Lunokhod 1 – the first remote-controlled vehicle on another celestial body.

luna21.text: Lunokhod 2 drove about 39 km – a record until 2014.

luna24.text: The last Soviet lunar mission; brought 170 g of drill core back to Earth.

change3.text: The first soft lunar landing in 37 years.

change4.text: First landing on the far side of the Moon. Radio contact with Earth only via the Queqiao relay satellite.

change5.text: Brought 1.7 kg of samples to Earth – the youngest lunar rock examined so far (≈ 2 billion years).

change6.text: First rock samples from the far side of the Moon (1.9 kg).

chandrayaan3.text: India became the fourth nation on the Moon – and the first near the south pole.

slim.text: Japan's "Moon sniper" landed within about 10 m – though upside down.

im1.text: First private Moon landing; the lander tipped over onto its side.

blueghost1.text: First fully successful private Moon landing; it filmed a sunset on the Moon.

im2.text: Landed farther south than any previous mission, but tipped over in a crater.

viking1.text: First successful Mars landing: the lander worked for over six years and sent the first colour images of the surface.

viking2.text: Second Viking lander; its camera showed frost on the Martian ground for the first time.

pathfinder.text: Brought the first rover to Mars with "Sojourner" and landed – airbag-cushioned – in an outflow plain.

spirit.text: Was to work for 90 days and drove for over six years, until it got stuck in soft sand (2010).

opportunity.text: Drove almost 45 km – a record for a non-Earth vehicle – and found signs of previously flowing water. Contact was lost in 2018 after a dust storm.

phoenix.text: Dug in the polar north and confirmed water ice close beneath the Martian surface.

curiosity.text: Since 2012 the nuclear-powered rover has been exploring Mount Sharp inside the Gale crater and found organic molecules and traces of an ancient lake.

insight.text: A stationary lander with a seismometer: it recorded over 1 300 Marsquakes and measured the structure of the planet's interior.

zhurong.text: China's first Mars landing succeeded on the first attempt; the rover drove about 1.9 km.

space.notYet: {name} does not exist yet at the chosen point in time (or its position is unknown).
space.satsError: Satellite data (CelesTrak) could not be loaded.
space.notLanded: At the chosen point in time, nobody has landed here yet.
space.satNote: Orbit data: CelesTrak. On the weather map (layer "Satellites") the ground track is visible as well.
space.overlaysNote: Overlays sit semi-transparent on top of the chosen map. Regional ones (minerals) apply only inside their footprint.
space.siteModelNote: Zooming in shows the 3D model of the lander{flags} and vehicles – enlarged so you can spot it, scaling with the zoom.
space.roverNote: The line shows the route driven so far (NASA MMGIS), the dot the last known position. Zooming in shows the 3D model – enlarged and scaling with the zoom.
space.heliNote: Ingenuity flew 72 times between April 2021 and January 2024. The dot marks the last landing site.

fp.testPushSent: Test notification is on its way.
fp.testPushFailed: Test failed – is the push service reachable?
fp.notesWhenClosed: You also receive the notifications while the app is closed.
fp.tripNotInTimetable: The trip was not found in the timetable (no service that day or the line has changed).

fp.departuresUnreachable: Departures unreachable – please try again later.
fp.notificationsOn: Notifications are on – you will be notified 30 and 10 min before departure.
